package_info.package_versions: unknown (all versions published to public npm under this name)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is considered malicious because it is a namespace-squatting attack: a malicious actor publishes a package with the same name as a proprietary internal package ('piedpiper-middle-out') to a public repository (npm). This can trick organizations into installing the malicious public package instead of their legitimate internal one, potentially leading to code execution, data exfiltration, or other attacks.

execution_context.trigger: import-time or install-time (when the package is installed or required by a developer)
execution_context.file_location: index.js (or main entry point of the malicious npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This code exfiltrates environment variables from the victim's system to an attacker-controlled server when the package is installed or imported.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code sends sensitive environment data to an external server without user consent, which is a common data exfiltration technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate package should not exfiltrate environment variables or make unsolicited network requests during install or import.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may send telemetry, but this should be opt-in and clearly documented.
key_indicators: Unsolicited network requests to external domains

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious package named 'piedpiper-middle-out' to the public npm registry, mimicking the internal proprietary package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Developers may accidentally install the malicious public package instead of the internal one.

attack_chain.action: Developer or CI system installs the malicious package from the public npm registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in the package is executed during install or import.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes, exfiltrating environment variables or other sensitive data to an attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive information, potentially leading to further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Packages with names matching known internal/proprietary namespaces published to public registries
Unexpected network requests during install or import
Access to environment variables or sensitive files in package code
file_indicators: index.js or main entry file containing network exfiltration code
package.json with suspicious or minimal metadata
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unknown or attacker-controlled domains during install/import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation of packages from public registries that match internal/proprietary package names. Analyze package code for unsolicited network requests or access to sensitive data. Use repository routing rules to block requests for internal namespaces from public proxies. Alert on any package that attempts to exfiltrate environment variables or other sensitive information during install or import.
